newsitem.title: CHINA: China B shares end mixed, sentiment uncertain.
newsitem.headline: China B shares end mixed, sentiment uncertain.

text.p: China's B share indices ended mixed on Tuesday with Shanghai shares falling on a disappointing showing by a new listing and Shenzhen edging up on institutional demand for recent large-capitalisation issues, brokers said.
Shanghai's foreign currency B shares ended down with market sentiment hurt by the unsatisfactory performance of newly-listed Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle Co and falls on the A share market, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index fell 1.512 points or 1.77 percent to 83.707, while Shenzhen B shares inched up 0.58 points or 0.39 percent to end at 149.70.
In Shanghai, Jinan Qingqi's 230 million B shares, listed today, ended the session at an intraday low of $0.55, compared with an issue price of $0.48.

"Qinqi's listing made most investors offset their positions in other shares to speculate in the newcomer, which pushed the market down," said one broker. "Falls among the A shares also hurt market sentiment."
Shares are not included in the index calculations on their first day of listing.
"The market's short-term outlook is not optimistic due to a lack of fresh capital and instability in the A share market," said another broker.
Shanghai A shares moved down after gains over the past few trading days, with a recent spate of listings and issues sucking capital out of the seconday market, brokers said.
The A index closed down 16.01 points or 1.22 percent to 1,301.12 points on volume of 305.8 million shares worth 4.0 billion yuan ($482.3 million).
In Shenzhen, the B share index erased early losses to end marginally higher in sluggish trade, boosted by institutional demand for recently listed large-capitalisation issues, brokers said.
"Institutional demand for newly-listed B shares lifted the B share index despite the poor performance of cheap-priced shares," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"Newcomers, which are mostly large-capitalised and have a solid earnings record, are likely to remain the target of buying for some time," the analyst said.

Shenzhen's domestic currency A share index fell 8.72 points or 1.97 percent to 434.40, ending a brief rally that started last Friday after heavy losses caused by Beijing's latest move to crack down on over-speculation, brokers said.
Shenzhen B shares would probably fluctuate in a tight band later this week, with the direction of their A share counterparts unclear, brokers said.
They said the A share market was driven down on Tuesday by selling from banks as the Friday deadline for them to unwind their equity positions approached.
"With the ban on state banks and enterprises and listed firms trading shares, the market will have difficulty rising strongly," an analyst with Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Shenzhen's A share market early this year experienced a bull-run which was stopped dead in its tracks in May by a string of crackdown measures launched by Beijing. ($ = 8.293 Chinese Yuan)
